There are words one keeps so deep within that they become a poison to the soul — words so dear to the heart's ear, and yet strangely absent from the lips. Stricken by this poison I address you, with the slowness of one who, at last, recognizes a feature glimpsed in a dream from before time: the splendor of your being.
 
I was taught that love is born of causes — of a glance, of a conversation, of a complicity built stone by stone. But you came without preamble, without permission, without my being able to raise the slightest wall of reason between your breath and mine. I love you without why. Not because you would suit me, not because the world allows it. I love you as one loves the morning light: because it is there, and without it, all would be false and lifeless. 

Sometimes I look at you and wonder if our souls have not already greeted each other elsewhere — in a forgotten tongue, beneath a sky of another color, with other names upon our lips. This shiver of recognition I feel in your presence does not belong to the short time of this life. It has the patience of things that wait centuries to find each other again.
 
You need not be perfect. You need not armor yourself in any shape but the one you wear when your eyes first find mine. It is there, in that unguarded nakedness, that I love you most — in that hollow of silence where even the ghosts of who we were before seem to kneel, to touch, to know each other again. 


I ask nothing of you. I promise nothing more than this raw truth: that somewhere, in the folds of eternity, I have already chosen to love you. And that I would do so again, without hesitation, in every life, beneath every sky, with every name you might bear.

No tears were permitted to fall behind his steel visor; a knight could not tarnish his lord’s joyful day with his own private grief.
​Late that night, high atop the cold and desolate watchtower, the knight gazed at the frozen stars above. His love would remain his greatest secret—a devotion without the hope of possession, a love that existed solely as a silent, unwavering guard.
